accepted.evidence: Andersen's jān- 'to know' head compares RV and Pali jānāti and records the Ashokan optative jāneyu/jānevu. Turner 5193 jānā́ti 'knows' lists Pali jānāti and Ashokan imperative jānaṁtu/future jānisaṁti, confirming the same present stem.

Andersen's likʰ- 'to write' head compares RV √likh and Pali likhati, with Ashokan causative likhāpayatha and participial likhite/likhitaṁ. Turner 11048 likháti 'scratches; writes' lists Pali likhati and Ashokan causatives likhapeśami/likhāpisaṁ plus 'will write' likhiyisāmi.

held.reason: Andersen's vas- head supplies Sanskrit/Pali comparison and compound cross-references but no independent inscriptional form on the printed page. Turner 11435 gives direct Ashokan vasati, but the installed source record may be a cross-reference stem rather than an observed lexical item.
